paragraphs.text: Pest is a creature type used for cards that depict small, destructive creatures. It is mostly used on tokens .
Pests are most prominent in black and green , though Signal Pest and the pest tokens created by Nuisance Engine were colorless artifact creatures
Pests were introduced as artifact creature tokens generated by Nuisance Engine in Mirrodin . The subtype returned in Mirrodin Besieged with the first non-token pest, Signal Pest .

Pests were reintroduced as non-artifact creatures in Strixhaven: School of Mages . They were created because R&D wanted a creature type for each College to act as its mascot . There wasn't a simple vanilla or French vanilla creature that worked for black-green , so they came up with creatures called Grubs that would see print as Pests. Mechanically, these were 1/1 creatures wit "When this creature dies , you gain 1 life," Witherbloom had a "life matters" mechanical theme, and this allowed their creature token type to play into that theme.
Pests, like Fractals , were excluded from the Mascot Exhibition partly due to power constraints, but largely because of the amount of text required to fit their lifegain ability.

For the return to Arcavios , Secrets of Strixhaven , the rules text for Pest tokens was changed to "Whenever this token attacks , you gain 1 life". R&D thought that this new version would lead to better gameplay.
Even amongst the archaic workings of Mirrodin's machines, the Nuisance Engine 's only discernible purpose was frustration.

At Strixhaven , pests are a sort of magical experiment gone feral. They were designed to be a fuel source for essence work, and live as a sort of side effect. Witherbloom students use them as mascots .

Witherbloom mages need life essence to channel their magic, and the creatures that most frequently do the job are simply called pests. Pests are salamander -like, generally irritating creatures that dissolve readily into magical power for Witherbloom spells. This is reflected by their death trigger that gains a life. They are wart-ridden, cold and slimy, and flagrantly violate decorum around manners and personal hygiene. Most mages outside of Witherbloom think of pests as awful creatures: they are disagreeable, hissing, spiky, untrainable monsters that bite without hesitation. But Witherbloom mages often carry pests around, doting on them as pets, pets that also serve as convenient sources of life essence.

Snarlflowers are a primary food source for the pests, which chew them down to the root, keeping the fast-growing vines from doing serious damage to the masonry of the University. When given a taste of bone, pests may become habituated to it. As pests are repositories for magical energy, it is conjectured that their essences are as primordial as elementals and that they may be related to every living thing on Arcavios. One of the simplest spells taught to all Witherbloom students drew forth the magical essence of a pest, converting it, body and soul, into pure magic. It is unclear whether these creatures are reptilian, insectoid, or other, as they are rarely grown past their larval stage. As such, their intelligence and mature forms are generally unknown and unseen, save for one precocious specimen of Blex .
During the New Phyrexian Invasion , some pests escaped captivity during the attack, letting them grow more than anticipated .
